title: Germany – Planting and maintenance services of green areas – Unterhaltspflege Elbauenpark Magdeburg in 3 Losen
description: Es ist beabsichtigt, die Pflegeleistungen für den Elbauenpark in Magdeburg für einen Zeitraum von einem Jahr (Anlage Plan) unterschiedlicher Größe und unterschiedlichen Leistungsumfanges zu vergeben. Der Auftragnehmer erhält die Option einer Verlängerung des Vertrages um jeweils ein weiteres Jahr bis zu einer Gesamtlaufzeit von maximal 4 Jahren. Der Vertrag verlängert sich jeweils um ein weiteres Jahr, wenn er nicht mit einer Frist von mindestens 12 Wochen zum Ablauf des jeweiligen Vertragsjahres schriftlich gekündigt wird; einer Begründung bedarf es nicht. Einzelheiten der Verlängerungsoption regeln der Bekanntmachungstext und der Vertragsentwurf. Für die Vergütung wird eine Lohnpreisgleitklausel vereinbart; Erhöhungen von Tariflöhnen und gesetzlichem Mindestlohn werden entsprechend berücksichtigt. Es wird ausdrücklich darauf hingewiesen, dass für alle in diesem Leistungsverzeichnis aufgeführten Arbeiten die Beschäftigung von Subunternehmen ausgeschlossen ist (Ausnahme Baumpflege und Inspektion und Wartungskontrolle Spiel - und Sportgeräte nach DIN EN 1176). Vor Kalkulation und Abgabe eines Angebotes wird auf die unbedingt hierfür erforderliche Begehung und Begutachtung des Pflegeobjektes hingewiesen, um sich über die örtlichen Gegebenheiten entsprechend umfassend und ausreichend zu informieren. Nachforderungen die auf Unkenntnis der grundlegenden Situation vor Ort basieren, werden nicht berücksichtigt und zurückgewiesen. Die Arbeiten erfordern Einsatz, Präsenz und Leistungsbereitschaft der Firmen vor Ort (Montag bis Freitag, s. Ausführungen). Die Vorgaben der DIN 18 919 sind Grundlage der Pflegearbeiten im Elbauenpark und werden im Folgenden präzisiert. Für den Bereich des Kleinen Cracauer Angers wurde 2014 ein Pflegehandbuch erstellt. Der Große Cracauer Anger besteht aus 14 einzelnen Pflegebereichen, nach denen die Einteilung der einzelnen Pflegeleistungen und der anteiligen Mengen und Flächen ermittelt wurden. Die Beschreibung der Pflegeleistungen dient als fachtechnischen Pflegegrundlage. Die dargestellten Pflegeintervalle sind ausschließlich Regelannahmen. Das Pflegehandbuch kann in der Verwaltung des Elbauenparks eingesehen werden.

title: France – Electronic components – Fourniture et livraison de composants électroniques pour le Groupe RATP
description: La présente consultation vise à conclure un accord cadre qui porte sur la livraison de composants électroniques pour la RATP : Répartie en deux lots : -Lot 1 : Fournitures de composants électroniques standards -Lot 2 : Fourniture de composants électroniques à approvisionnement complexe Pour chaque lot, le marché qui sera conclu à l’issu de la consultation sera un accord-cadre à bons de commandes mono-attributaire, établi sans montant minimum et avec un montant maximum (+50% du montant médian pour lot 1 / +30% du montant médian pour le lot 2 ). title: Ireland – Grounds maintenance services – Provision of routine maintenance services for licenced landfill sites in County Donegal
description: Donegal County Council is required to maintain compliance with the terms and conditions of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Waste Licences for its closed landfills. This project covers Balbane, Ballinacarrick and Dungloe Landfill Sites. The successful contractor will perform routine maintenance to ensure clear access to pollution control infrastructure and compliance monitoring locations. The contractor must execute the core activities of Grass cutting and Vegetation Clearance with on-site mulching, and Litter Removal within the site boundaries. Other Ad-Hoc services may from time to time include repair or replacement of boundary health and safety signage, minor repairs to permanent fencing, access gates and stiles, shrub clearance, brush cutting.

title: Intent to sole source Bridge contract Waste MGT
description: Notice of intent to award a sole source bridge contract. This is not a solicitation. The Department of Veterans Affairs intends to negotiate a sole source contract for 8 Month Base with DBI Waste Systems INC 377 3rd st Everett MA for the VA Healthcare Rhode Island to obtain Waste and Recycling pickup/disposal. While procuring a new Base plus 4 option years contract. The current contract 36C24121D0009 ends on 9/30/2026 with no contractual ability to extend. The current RFQ 36C24126Q0580 did not result in an award in time to prevent a lapse in service due to a Protest. The RFQ was protested twice; the most recent protest was dismissed on 8/19/2026, with VA taking corrective action. A new RFQ is being developed for a base plus 4 option years. This sole source bridge contract with the current vendor will continue service without interruption or risk of service while the new RFQ is being developed. No other contractor can be installed before the contract expiration date without creating a critical service delay. Which would result in hazardous accumulation of waste at the facility, creating unsanitary conditions, pest and fire hazards, and infection control risks, and potential noncompliance with VHA Directive 1850.06, Waste Management Program, and VHA Directive 1850.01, Health Care Environmental Services. DBI Waste Systems, as the incumbent, already has the equipment, staff, and site-specific knowledge in place under the existing contract, allowing performance to continue immediately without the added risk of transitioning to an unproven provider during this critical period. Since the intent is to procure this on a sole source basis, no solicitation will be posted to FedBizOps (FBO). The applicable NAICS code is 562111 Solid Waste Collection with a $47 Million Size Standard. The PSC is S205. The authority for this action is FAR 6.302-2 Unusual and Compelling Urgency due to not being able to award a new Base + 4 option years from RFQ 36C24126Q0133 and 36C24126Q0580. Performance Work statement synopsis contractor shall be responsible for allocating all equipment and personnel, including back-up resources, to meet all requirements for the comprehensive management of the solid waste and recycling programs for the VAMC Rhode Island Healthcare System. The comprehensive waste services shall not only include the collection, recycling and disposal of waste, but also the training and support required to ensure compliance with all Federal, State, and Local regulations. Interested persons may contact the Contracting Specialist via email at James.Moore14@va.gov regarding this procurement. The determination to conduct a competitive procurement based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Contracting Officer.

title: 3910--764_Conveyors_VA CMOP Murfreesboro EF_36C77026Q0181 Tote packing addition. SS to QMSI
description: PURPOSE: SPECIAL NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE PROCUREMENT � PRESOLICITATION NOTICE (RFO 5.101) THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR QUOTE. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION. THE VA IS NOT CURRENTLY SEEKING QUOTES/OFFERS/PROPOSALS AND WILL NOT ACCEPT UNSOLICITED PROPOSALS. THIS IS A NOTICE OF THE GOVERNMENT'S INTENT TO ISSUE A SOLE SOURCE AWARD PREPARED IN ACCORDANCE WITH RFO 5.101, PRESOLICITATION NOTICE. Contracting Office: Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office 15 (NCO 15) � CMOP Division, 3450 S. 4th St. Trafficway, Leavenworth, KS 66048-5012. Point of Contact: Michael W. McAlhaney, Contracting Officer, Michael.McAlhaney@va.gov. Product/Service Code: 3910 (Conveyors). NAICS Code: 333922 (Conveyor and Conveying Equipment Manufacturing). Set-Aside Status: This action is not a small business set-aside under FAR Part 19. QMSI is registered as a small business under NAICS 333922; however, this action is being conducted as a sole-source award under the "only one responsible source" authority described below, not as a Part 19 set-aside. This Notice announces that the Department of Veterans Affairs, Consolidated Mail Outpatient Pharmacy (CMOP), Station 764, located in Murfreesboro, Tennessee, is proposing to negotiate a firm-fixed-price contract with Quality Manufacturing Systems, Inc. (QMSI), a small business, on a sole-source basis, under the authority at 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1) as implemented by RFO 6.103-1 (Only One Responsible Source). The proposed action is for the modification of the existing tote conveyance and Automated Pharmacy Fulfillment System (APFS) at Mid-South CMOP. The modification will add semi-automated packer (SAP) capability to the existing tote line, including conversion of Labeling Spurs 9 and 10 into Pharmacist Verification (PV) spurs, conversion of PV Spurs 3 and 4 into manual packing stations, integration of three package takeaway conveyors, tote sorter and diagnostic screen updates, and installation of the associated control system hardware and software. The work also requires modification of station workload-balancing logic, additional infrastructure to support the new SAP station (including a pharmacy Ethernet drop and supporting utilities), and development of a Human-Machine Interface (HMI) application enabling independent operator control of puck conveyance separate from tote Hytrol conveyor operations. The APFS is designed using proprietary software developed by QMSI, including the semi-automated packing machine software, product routing, and machine interface software. This software cannot be modified by any entity other than QMSI. QMSI is the only vendor with full knowledge of the overall system design, workload allocation logic, and the interaction between the tote conveyance, PLC/HMI controls, and APFS subsystems. Basis for Lack of Competition: Competition is not being sought because QMSI is the sole source possessing the proprietary knowledge, technical capability, and authorized access necessary to modify, integrate, validate, and warrant the existing QMSI-proprietary software, controls, and APFS integration at this facility. This determination is documented in the Government's market research report and single-source justification for Acquisition Plan 36C770-26-AP-0637. Invitation to Respond: Any firm believing it possesses the proprietary authorization and technical capability to perform the required software integration, controls modification, and APFS-compatible work described above is invited to submit a written capability statement demonstrating such ability. Capability statements must be received no later than 09/29/2026 and submitted via email to Michael.McAlhaney@va.gov. Any capability statement received will be considered by the Government in determining whether to proceed with the intended sole-source award to QMSI. This is not a request for quotes. Interested parties may also notify NCO 15 of their ability to provide similar upgrades for future needs.

title: Waste MGT and Recycling Intent to Sole source
description: Notice of intent to award a sole source bridge contract. This is not a solicitation. The Department of Veterans Affairs intends to negotiate a sole source contract for 8 Month Base with DBI Waste Systems INC 377 3rd st Everett MA for the VA Healthcare Bedford to obtain Waste and Recycling pickup/disposal. While procuring a new Base plus 4 option years contract. The current contract 36C24121D0009 ends on 9/30/2026 with no contractual ability to extend. The current RFQ 36C24126Q0577 did not result in an award in time to prevent a lapse in service due to a Protest. The RFQ was protested twice; the most recent protest was dismissed on 8/19/2026, with VA taking corrective action. A new RFQ is being developed for a base plus 4 option years. This sole source bridge contract with the current vendor will continue service without interruption or risk of service while the new RFQ is being developed. No other contractor can be installed before the contract expiration date without creating a critical service delay. Which would result in hazardous accumulation of waste at the facility, creating unsanitary conditions, pest and fire hazards, and infection control risks, and potential noncompliance with VHA Directive 1850.06, Waste Management Program, and VHA Directive 1850.01, Health Care Environmental Services. DBI Waste Systems, as the incumbent, already has the equipment, staff, and site-specific knowledge in place under the existing contract, allowing performance to continue immediately without the added risk of transitioning to an unproven provider during this critical period. Since the intent is to procure this on a sole source basis, no solicitation will be posted to FedBizOps (FBO). The applicable NAICS code is 562111 Solid Waste Collection with a $47 Million Size Standard. The PSC is S205. The authority for this action is FAR 6.302-2 Unusual and Compelling Urgency due to not being able to award a new Base + 4 option years from RFQ 36C24126Q0133 and 36C24126Q0577. Performance Work statement synopsis contractor shall be responsible for allocating all equipment and personnel, including back?up resources, to meet all requirements for the comprehensive management of the solid waste and recycling programs for the VAMC Bedford Healthcare System. The comprehensive waste services shall not only include the collection, recycling and disposal of waste, but also the training and support required to ensure compliance with all Federal, State, and Local regulations. Interested persons may contact the Contracting Specialist via email at James.Moore14@va.gov regarding this procurement. The determination to conduct a competitive procurement based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Contracting Officer.

title: Piflufolastat F-18 injection drugs (Pylarify) from Lantheus (Notice of Intent to sole source)
description: Acquisition Description: This is a Notice of Intent, not a request for proposal. The National Institute of Health, Clinical Center (NIH-CC) intends to negotiate on an other than full and open competition basis with Progenics Pharmaceuticals Inc. The National Institute of Health, Clinical Center (NIH-CC)�s has the Nuclear Pharmacy (CC NP) department (collectively �Program�) that purchases and compounds radiopharmaceuticals (radioactive drugs) on a daily basis for life-saving clinical nuclear medicine procedures. This is essential for the NIH Clinical Center to achieve optimal patient care. These radiopharmaceuticals are United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved drugs for use in patients. They are also radioactive materials that are regulated by the United States Nuclear Regulatory Commission (US NRC) through the NIH radioactive material license (RAM) administered by the NIH Radiation Safety Office (RSO). Only RSO certified Nuclear Medicine personnel can order these radiopharmaceuticals directly for patient use. Each radiopharmaceutical is time sensitive because of the rapid radiation decay. Because of their short useful half-lives, they cannot be ordered in advance for storage. They must be properly compounded, dispensed, calibrated and delivered for a specific patient at a specific time on a specific date on a daily basis. The purpose is to procure compounded piflufolasta F-18 in patient ready unit doses (UDs) from an authorized nuclear pharmacy for the use by the NIH Nuclear Medicine, Department of Radiology and Imaging Sciences to diagnose and treat diseases as required by necessary patient care protocols at the NIH Clinical Center. This new radioactive drug is vital to the NIH Clinical Center mission. The product is owned and developed by Lantheus Medical/Progenics Pharmaceuticals (now merged as one company). Progenics Pharmaceuticals Inc uses Lantheus� Federal Supply Schedule contract on contract 36F79719D0170. Justification and other information: This requirement will be sole sourced to Progenics Pharmaceuticals Inc. under FAR 8.405-6 (b): Only one source is capable of providing the supplies or services required at the level of quality required because the supplies or services are unique or highly specialized. This notice is being made on SAM.gov instead of GSA Ebuy because the GSA Ebuy category �65 I B PHARMACEUTICALS AND DRUGS� states that �This SIN is not available through GSA Advantage.� Lantheus Medical Imaging (a company of Lanntheus Holding, Inc.) is the developer and intellectual property owner of Piflufolastat F-18 injection drugs (Pylarify) in the United States. More specifically, Progenics Pharmceuticals had been developing this drug and Lantheus merged Progenics Pharmaceuticals. Progenics Pharmaceuticals Inc is the only local authorized commercial nuclear pharmacy authorized by Lanthesus Medical Imaging to compound, prepare, delivery and invoice for these drugs. They use the Federal Supply Schedule contract on contract 36F79719D0170, and they are the designated authorized vendor for our area. Only this drug can be used for Program�s patient care and research and Program has been using these drugs for years in ongoing projects and patient care. Only qualified vendors that meet the FDA and US NRC regulations can provide these radiopharmaceuticals for compounding and dispensing at NIH Nuclear Pharmacy to NIH Clinical Center patients. Thus, only Progenics Pharmaceuticals Inc. is the sole authorized provider of these drugs. Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Requirement: 150x to 230x Qty of PYLARIFY piflufolastat F-18 injections 4x Qty for PYLARIFY unused doses fees Base Year Option Year 1 Option Year 2 Option Year 3 Option Year 4 Place of Performance or Delivery: The contract period of performance is 10/01/2026 � 09/30/2027 for the base year. Option Years: 10/01/2027 � 09/30/2028 10/01/2028 � 09/30/2029 10/01/2029 � 09/30/2030 10/01/2030 � 09/30/2031 This requirement will be awarded on GSA Contract #36F79719D0170. Place of Performance: NIH Clinical Center in Bethesda, MD The statutory authority for this sole source requirement is 41 U.S.C. 1901 (a) (1) as implemented by FAR 13.106-1 and/or FAR 8.405-6 - only one responsible source and no other supply of service will satisfy agency requirements. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. All responsible sources that could provide the required may submit a capability statement that will be considered by email (subject line to reference NOI-000004) by 10:00 AM eastern standard time on 09/29/2026 to: lu-chang.lu@nih.gov All responses received by the closing date of this synopsis will be considered by the Government. A determination not to compete this requirement, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government.

description: De gemeente Ede wenst de exploitatie van deelauto's in Ede-Centrum en elektrische deelbakfietsen in de hele gemeente Ede in de markt te leggen middels concessies. Met deze concessies beoogt de gemeente een kwalitatief, toekomstbestendig en toegankelijk aanbod van deelauto’s en elektrische deelbakfietsen te realiseren, passend bij de ruimtelijke ontwikkeling van het centrumgebied en de mobiliteitsopgaven van de gemeente. In verband met de verschillende markten en de verschillende concessiegebieden voor deelauto’s en elektrische bakfietsen kiest de gemeente ervoor om deze concessies middels twee aanbestedingen uit te vragen: één voor elektrische deelbakfietsen en één voor deelauto's. Deze aanbesteding betreft de aanbesteding deelauto's. De opdracht betreft de concessie voor de exploitatie van deelauto’s binnen het werkingsgebied van het Mobiliteitsfonds, zoals weergegeven in bijlage 2. title: Ireland – Roadworks – DCC Contract for Construction of the Coolock to Clontarf Active Travel Scheme Section 2 – Gracefield Road to Vernon Avenue
description: Dublin City Council aims to enhance the quality of life for its residents by developing an integrated Active Travel Network. This comprehensive network is designed to foster connections among individuals via pedestrian pathways, segregated cycle provision and other environmentally friendly transportation alternatives. The enhancement of accessibility and interconnectivity for people walking, wheeling and cycling within this network is anticipated to play a pivotal role in mitigating carbon emissions originating from transport activities. The Council’s objective is to augment the existing 40km network into a seamlessly connected 314km network spanning the entire city. The Gracefield Road to Vernon Avenue Active Travel Scheme is one of the projects identified under this initiative. Gracefield Road, Brookwood Avenue, Sybil Hill Road and Vernon Avenue have been identified as suitable roads for active travel measures. This scheme will deliver protected cycling facilities in both directions and numerous improvements for pedestrians over a 2.6km route along these roads, between the junctions with Malahide Road and Seafield Road. The scheme includes the provision of segregated cycle facilities, improved pedestrian facilities (footpath and junction upgrades), ducting, resurfacing, etc.. The scheme also includes the upgrade of seven signal-controlled junctions to improve pedestrian and cyclist facilities. The scheme comprises the following: - Reconfiguration of existing carriageway for inclusion of protected cycle lanes - Site clearance - Pavement works - Kerbs and footways - Traffic islands - Public lighting - Traffic signs and road markings - Drainage works - Traffic signals and ducting - Utilities - Landscaping and urban realm works - Bike stands - Temporary traffic management. For further information, please refer to documentation available to download from www.etenders.gov.ie; CfT ID 8916766. Please note that this project is subject to funding.

title: Notice Of Intent To Sole Source - LRS Bus Engine Repair Service
description: THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS/QUOTES The 97th CON Squadron at Altus, OK 73523 intends to solicit and negotiate a sole-source, firm-fixed-price contract for the acquisition of bus engine repair. The 97th Contracting Squadron intends to make award this contract to RUSH TRUCK CENTERS OF TEXAS, LP (CAGE: 99MX9). This acquisition is being conducted as a noncompetitive contract action under the authority of Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Overhaul (RFO) 6.103-1: "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements". The 97 LRS/LGRV requires the complete replacement of a failed 8.3L L6 Cummins ISC diesel engine on a government-owned 2009 Bluebird Bus. This specialized vehicle is a critical "1-of-1" asset utilized on Altus AFB for flightline aircrew transport, off-base logistical missions, and military Commercial Driver's License (CDL) training. The vehicle suffered catastrophic internal engine failure during transit and is currently inoperable, occupying space at the Rush Truck Centers facility. In accordance with RFO 6.103-1 the Government has restricted competition due to severe logistical and cost constraints. Because the vehicle is entirely non-operational, soliciting competition from alternative regional mechanics is highly impractical. Transporting the bus would force the Government to incur immediate, non-recoverable heavy-duty towing expenses and redundant diagnostic teardown fees at a secondary facility, directly offsetting any potential savings from competition. This notice of intent is NOT a request for competitive proposals and no solicitation document exists for the requirement. Sources interested in responding to this notice are required to submit a capability statement that includes technical data and cost information, sufficient detail and with convincing evidence that clearly demonstrates the capability to meet the requirement. Requests for documentation, additional information, or submissions that only ask questions will not be considered as an affirmative response. A determination by the Government not to compete based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement or to proceed with a single source procurement. Capability statements are due on 09/29/2026 by 10:00 AM CST. Capability statements shall be submitted by email ONLY as a Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF attachment to phillip.chambers.4@us.af.mil and ryan.lafever.2@us.af.mil. Capability statements and supporting documentation provided after the due date listed above will not be reviewed. Please see attached Single Source Justification for further information.

title: CGC HEALY FIRE DETECTION SYSTEM OVERHAUL
description: The United States Coast Guard Deputy Commandant for Systems (DCS) is issuing this combined synopsis/solicitation on behalf of the Surface Forces Logistics Center (SFLC) to award a firm-fixed-price fire detection system overhaul contract, as detailed in the attached Statement of Work. This requirement consists of performing all on-site labor and services to fire detection system overhaul in support of the USCGC HEALY. All work must be performed on-site at 1519 Alaskan Way S Seattle WA, 98134. The period of performance for this work starts upon award and in collaboration with the COR, with an end date of no later than October 16, 2026.. This acquisition is a 100% total small business set-aside under NAICS code 334290, with a corresponding small business size standard of 800. The applicable Product Service Code is 6350. The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose quote conforming to the solicitation is most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following factors will be used to evaluate offers: Technical Capability (Pass/Fail) Past Performance (Pass/Fail) Total Price A quotation must receive an Acceptable rating for all non-price factors to be eligible for award. Among all acceptable quotations, award will be made to the responsible offeror submitting the lowest evaluated price. To establish Technical Capability (Pass/Fail), the quotation must demonstrate a clear understanding of the work statement requirements, conform strictly to all specifications in the attached Statement of Work, and provide any adequate capability and corporate experience documentation required by the solicitation. Failure to meet these criteria will render the quotation unacceptable. The Government will evaluate recent (completed within the last three years) and relevant past performance to assess the likelihood of successful performance. Past performance will be evaluated on an acceptable or unacceptable basis. To receive an acceptable rating, past performance must demonstrate a rating of satisfactory or higher performance of similar work. Offerors without recent or relevant past performance will be assessed as "Neutral" and considered acceptable for award. Past performance demonstrating marginal or below performance is unacceptable. Offerors shall identify all subcontractors anticipated to perform work under this contract. For each subcontractor, the offeror shall provide the subcontractor�s name, address, point of contact, phone number, the specific work items/specifications they will perform, and the percentage of work they will execute. Submit offers electronically via email to the points of contact identified in this notice. The Government does not prescribe a specific quotation format. Offerors must submit a quotation that clearly identifies the items offered and demonstrates compliance with the stated requirements. Submissions must be complete, clear, and presented in a format that allows effective evaluation by the Government. Submit all questions via email to the points of contact identified in this notice. The Government will not accept telephone inquiries. Submit offers on a firm-fixed-price basis. Prices must be all-inclusive and must cover all costs associated with providing the fire detection system overhaul contract, including but not limited to manufacturing, packaging, handling, transportation, duties, tariffs, fees, and any other costs. The Government may consider offers nonresponsive if they include conditional pricing, price escalation language, or statements indicating that prices are subject to adjustment based on future costs or fees. The Government intends to evaluate offers and make award without discussions; therefore, offerors should submit their best offer with initial submission. The Statement of Work and the list of applicable FAR provisions and clauses are attached to this notice.

(1) The Contractor must provide an itemized breakdown for changes exceeding the micro-purchase threshold (see FAR 2.101). (2) The itemized breakdown shall include materials, quantities, unit prices, labor costs (separated into trades), construction equipment, etc. Labor costs shall be identified with specific material placed or operation performed. (3) Proposals shall be submitted to the Contracting Officer or ACO and the resident engineer as expeditiously as possible, but not later than 10 calendar days, after receipt of a written change order by the Contracting Officer. title: Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women Infants and Children
description: The project is expected to be conducted in two phases. During Phase I, the contractor shall review all relevant scientific literature to ensure that the WIC food packages are scientifically based; assess current science on the nutritional needs of the WIC target population; review information on the dietary intake of WIC participants; and examine public health concerns and issues surrounding different types of eating patterns. As part of this process, the contractor shall convene an expert committee and conduct no less than six expert committee meetings. In addition, the contractor shall conduct not less than two full day public forums to gather professional and public input. At the conclusion of Phase I, the contractor shall issue a Phase I Report that provides an assessment of the nutritional needs of the WIC population relative to current nutritional science, a discussion of how well the current WIC food packages address these needs within the supplemental framework, modeling and analyses to be conducted in Phase II, and a preview of the Phase II recommendation development process. Phase II will include a Phase II Report containing detailed documentation of all findings and specific recommendations for changes in the foods and amounts of food provided in the WIC food packages for each of the various types of WIC food packages. The recommendations for each of the packages should be supported by a discussion of the nutritional rationale (including but not limited to discussion of the latest nutritional science and other expert recommendations), a food group and subgroup and nutrient analysis, and estimated annual costs or savings compared to baseline of the individual food changes. In addition, the recommendations for all the packages should be presented as a recommendation supported by an estimate of the annual cost or savings and change from baseline. The recommendations may include options; however, the cost of each recommended set of changes shall be estimated separately for each food package.

title: USACE SPK Construction - Natomas PP5, Sacramento, CA
description: *** Amendment 0003 has been issued****** Amendment 0002 has been issued****** Amendment 0001 has been issued ***The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Sacramento District (SPK) is issuing a solicitation for the requirement to construct a new pumping plant facility in Sacramento, CA. The American River Common Features, Natomas Basin Project was authorized by the Water Resources Reform Development Act of 2014. The Natomas Basin is divided into nine reaches, A through I. Pumping Plant 5 (PP5) is in Reach B, located along the Sacramento River near the landside toe of the levee and south of Interstate 5. PP5 is designed to discharge drainage from the West Drainage Canal to the Sacramento River following any significant amount of rainfall. The existing PP5 is in the path of completing the Reach B levee improvements that includes seepage berm, adjacent levee, and raising discharge pipes above the 200-year water surface elevation. The existing PP5 will be demolished, and a new facility will be constructed about 300 feet up the canal to allow for the levee features to be constructed .Point of Contact: Antonina Beal, Contract Specialist. Email: Antonina.Beal@usace.army.mil. Please refer to the full solicitation document for all detailed instructions, clauses, and submission requirements.

title: 384-well Viaflo Head
description: 1.0 DESCRIPTION This is a Combined Synopsis/Solicitation for commercial products and commercial services conducted in accordance with RFO FAR Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services, using the simplified procedures applicable to commercial products and commercial services. This notice constitutes the solicitation. Quotations are requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. The National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS), Division of Translational Toxicology (DTT), Mechanistic Toxicology Branch (MTB), intends to acquire one 384-channel liquid-handling pipetting head with a 5�125 �L operating volume range for use with existing 96/384 liquid-handling equipment located at NIEHS. The Government is seeking a commercially available 384-channel pipetting head that meets the functional, performance, compatibility, and operational requirements described in the attached Requirements Document. The Government will consider quotations for products offered by all responsible sources that demonstrate compliance with all stated requirements. The Government's requirement is based on the functional and performance characteristics necessary to support the intended scientific application and compatibility with the Government's existing liquid-handling equipment and laboratory workflow. The requirement is not restricted to a particular manufacturer, make, or model. The Government requires a 384-channel liquid-handling pipetting head capable of supporting high-throughput liquid handling on 384-well culture plates within the required 5�125 �L volume range. The equipment will support ongoing translational toxicology research involving human-based microphysiological systems and advanced 3D cell models, including liver-focused research conducted through an NIH-funded collaboration with NCATS under a Complement-ARIE grant award. The required pipetting head shall be compatible with the existing 96/384 liquid-handling equipment at NIEHS and shall increase laboratory capacity for high-throughput liquid handling within the specified volume range. The equipment shall provide reliable and reproducible liquid handling suitable for the Government's intended laboratory applications. The requirement includes the 384-channel pipetting head and applicable installation, configuration, technical support, and user training necessary to place the equipment into operational service, as specified in the applicable quotation. Installation and training shall be coordinated with NIEHS laboratory personnel and shall provide sufficient instruction to enable designated personnel to operate the equipment effectively. The equipment shall operate independently of NIEHS information technology systems and shall not require integration with NIEHS enterprise information technology infrastructure or IT support. Acceptance shall be based on the Government's determination that the delivered pipetting head has been delivered, installed or configured as applicable, is compatible with the existing NIEHS 96/384 liquid-handling equipment, and successfully performs the required liquid-handling functions within the specified 5�125 �L volume range. NIEHS laboratory staff will verify functionality in coordination with appropriate technical scientific support. The Government anticipates awarding a firm-fixed-price purchase order to the responsible offeror whose quotation conforms to the solicitation requirements and whose price is determined fair and reasonable. The Government will consider quotations from all responsible sources capable of meeting the complete requirements. An offeror may propose any manufacturer's product that meets or exceeds the stated salient physical, functional, compatibility, and performance characteristics. Required delivery date: September 30, 2026 Delivery Location: NIEHS Rall Building 101, Laboratories E144-146 111 T.W. Alexander Drive Research Triangle Park, NC 27709 The applicable NAICS code is 334516 � Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing. The applicable PSC is 6630 � Chemical Analysis Instruments. Please see the attached Requirements Document for the detailed technical and performance requirements. Please see the attached requirements document titled �75N98026Q01256 � Requirements Document� for additional information. 2.0 TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS AND QUOTATION INFORMATION The Government is seeking a commercially available 384-channel liquid-handling pipetting head capable of satisfying the technical, functional, compatibility, operational, installation, and training requirements identified in this solicitation and the attached Requirements Document. Offerors may propose products manufactured by any responsible manufacturer. However, the proposed product must satisfy all mandatory requirements stated in the solicitation and Requirements Document. Each quotation shall identify: Manufacturer name; Product name and model number; Manufacturer part number; Country of manufacture of the proposed end product; Proposed product configuration; Operating volume range and 384-channel configuration; Compatibility with the Government's existing 96/384 liquid-handling equipment; Installation and training included in the quoted price, as applicable; Delivery schedule; and Sufficient technical documentation to demonstrate compliance with each mandatory requirement. Offerors shall provide sufficient technical information for the Government to determine whether the proposed product meets or exceeds each applicable requirement. Documentation shall clearly identify the proposed product's physical, functional, performance, and compatibility characteristics. The Government will evaluate proposed products based on their demonstrated ability to satisfy the stated functional, physical, performance, compatibility, and operational requirements. The Government will not evaluate products based on manufacturer identity, brand familiarity, or similarity to a particular manufacturer's commercial configuration except to the extent necessary to determine compliance with the stated requirements. BASIS FOR AWARD The Government intends to award a firm-fixed-price purchase order resulting from this solicitation. The Government will evaluate quotations based on: Technical Acceptability � The proposed product must meet all mandatory requirements identified in the Requirements Document. The Government will consider the offeror's technical description, manufacturer documentation, and other information submitted with the quotation. Price � The Government will evaluate the total quoted price, including all required equipment, components, delivery, installation, training, and other costs necessary to satisfy the requirements. title: Microencapsulation Fluidics System
description: 1.0 DESCRIPTION This is a Combined Synopsis/Solicitation for commercial products and commercial services conducted in accordance with RFO FAR Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services, using the simplified procedures applicable to commercial products and commercial services. This notice constitutes the solicitation. Quotations are requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. The National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS), Division of Translational Toxicology (DTT), Mechanistic Toxicology Branch (MTB), intends to acquire a commercially available microencapsulation fluidics system, including the required microfluidic modules, pumping and droplet-generation components, computer and software, installation, and training. The Government is seeking a commercially available system that meets the functional, performance, and operational requirements described in the attached Requirements Document. The Government will consider quotations for the named product as well as products offered by other manufacturers that demonstrate compliance with all stated requirements. The Government's requirement is based on the functional and performance characteristics necessary to support the intended scientific application and is not restricted to a particular manufacturer, make, or model. The Government requires a specialized microencapsulation fluidics platform capable of combining liquid-form alginate with human cell suspensions under controlled conditions and generating droplets that form alginate capsules around suspension cells. The system will support the formation of three-dimensional (3D) microtissues, organoids, spheroids, and other advanced cell models for translational toxicology applications. The required system shall provide controlled microfluidic pumping and droplet-generation capabilities suitable for the Government's intended application. The system shall permit reliable and reproducible combination of alginate and human cell suspensions and generation of appropriately sized droplets under controlled operating conditions. The requirement includes the system hardware, applicable control equipment, computer and software necessary for operation, installation, and user training. Installation and training shall be performed at the NIEHS facility and shall include sufficient instruction to enable designated laboratory personnel to operate the system and perform the required microencapsulation procedures. The system shall operate independently of NIEHS information technology systems and shall not require integration with NIEHS enterprise information technology infrastructure. Acceptance shall be based on the Government's determination that the delivered system has been installed and configured in accordance with the solicitation requirements and is capable of performing the specified microencapsulation process. Acceptance may include demonstration of successful formation of alginate-encapsulated human cell-containing microtissues using Government-provided materials. The Government anticipates awarding a firm-fixed-price purchase order to the responsible offeror whose quotation conforms to the solicitation requirements and whose price is determined fair and reasonable. The Government will consider quotations from all responsible sources capable of meeting the complete requirements. title: USACE SPK Construction - Natomas PP5, Sacramento, CA
description: *** Amendment 0004 has been issued ****** Amendment 0003 has been issued****** Amendment 0002 has been issued****** Amendment 0001 has been issued ***The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Sacramento District (SPK) is issuing a solicitation for the requirement to construct a new pumping plant facility in Sacramento, CA. The American River Common Features, Natomas Basin Project was authorized by the Water Resources Reform Development Act of 2014. The Natomas Basin is divided into nine reaches, A through I. Pumping Plant 5 (PP5) is in Reach B, located along the Sacramento River near the landside toe of the levee and south of Interstate 5. PP5 is designed to discharge drainage from the West Drainage Canal to the Sacramento River following any significant amount of rainfall. The existing PP5 is in the path of completing the Reach B levee improvements that includes seepage berm, adjacent levee, and raising discharge pipes above the 200-year water surface elevation. The existing PP5 will be demolished, and a new facility will be constructed about 300 feet up the canal to allow for the levee features to be constructed .Point of Contact: Antonina Beal, Contract Specialist. Email: Antonina.Beal@usace.army.mil. Please refer to the full solicitation document for all detailed instructions, clauses, and submission requirements.

title: 513 CVN MCS Seaport
description: --- The procurement is limited to SeaPort-NxG (Multiple Award Contract (MAC) holders only. This solicitation will be competed under the SeaPort-NxG MAC amongst all MAC holders on an unrestricted basis. --- The Naval Surface Warfare Center Philadelphia Division (NSWCPD), Code 513, requires contractual support for the provisioning of modernization-engineering, life cycle, and in-service engineering support to meet readiness and safety criteria. The support shall include computer program development, systems engineering, testing, equipment harvesting, integrated logistic support (ILS), waterfront support and installation for new ship construction and in service ships for CVN68 Class, CVN78 Class, Columbia Class, FF(X) Class, Amphibious ships, USCG cutters, and FMS vessels and other new ship classes. This support is applicable for Machinery Control Systems (MCS), Damage Control Systems, and Network Systems. The resulting award will be a Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF) SeaPort-NxG Task Order.

title: 7A21--(New Action): VA Procurement Policy Documentation Control Software (VA-27-00008195)
description: Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Document Control Management System SharePoint Online Integration Request for Information (RFI) Introduction This Request for Information (RFI) is issued for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation nor does it restrict the government as to the ultimate acquisition approach. In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The purpose of this RFI is to identify qualified vendors, who are able to meet the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) requirements for contractor support to modernize and optimize its warehouse operations. The objective of this requirement is to seek an enterprise-ready document control management solution designed to streamline the lifecycle of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), forms, and related reference materials. See draft Performance Work Statement. The Government is not responsible for any cost incurred by industry in furnishing this information. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested vendor's expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future Request for Proposal (RFP), if any is issued. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary. All submissions will become Government property and will not be returned. Interested vendors are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted or competition sensitive information contained in their response. RFI Response Instructions NOTE: The capability package must be clear, concise, and complete. VA is under no obligation to provide feedback to the company, or to contact the company for clarification of any information submitted in response to this RFI. Provide the following information: Provide Company Information: Company Name CAGE/DUNS Number under which the company is registered in SAM/VetBiz.gov Company Address Point of contact name Telephone number Email address For small business concerns, indicate whether at least 50 percent of the total amount paid by the Government will be paid to firms that are similarly situated. Brief summary describing your company s technical approach to meeting the requirements, to include: List any previous or existing contracts you have with the VA where similar work was performed to this requirement. Also, is there an existing contract vehicle you recommend be used for this procurement? Does the draft Product Description (PD) provide sufficient detail to describe the technical and functional requirements that encompass the requirement? If NO , please provide your technical and functional comments/recommendations/questions on elements of the draft outline that may contribute to a more accurate proposal submission and efficient, cost-effective effort. If your company is a Small Business, also include the following: The intent and ability to meet set-aside requirements for performance of this effort. Information as to proposed team members, the percentage of work each is to perform, and which PD requirements would be subcontracted. Responses are due at 1:00 PM EST, September 29, 2026. Submit your responses directly on GSA. Should you have any questions, please reach out to: Contract Specialist: Ana Subashi. ana.subashi@va.gov AND Contracting Officer: Kendra Casebolt. kendra.casebolt@va.gov All responsible sources may submit a response in accordance with the following: All proprietary/company confidential material shall be clearly marked on every page that contains such. Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB) and Veteran Owned Small Businesses (VOSB) must indicate whether at least 50% of the cost incurred would be expended for prime employees or employees of other eligible SDVOSB/VOSB firms. This should also include the prime planned percentage and if under 50%, the names of the potential team members that may be used to fulfill the 50% SDVOSB/VOSB requirement. Please keep your response to no more than 6 pages.

title: Bonneville Ultrasonic Flow Meter
description: COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION W9127N26QA166 Bonneville Ultrasonic Flow Meter Bonneville Lock and Dam U.S. ARMY CORPS OF ENGINEERS, PORTLAND DISTRICT 21 SEP 2026 This solicitation is for commercial supplies prepared in accordance with the format in the Revolutionary RFO 12.201-1 - Simplified Acquisition Procedures, and additional information is included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested. Solicitation W9127N26QA166 is for the purchase of one (1) Emerson Flexim FLUXUS G631EE Portable Gas Clamp on Ultrasonic Flow Meter System, complete with required accessories, clamp-on transducers, and specialized probes. This requirement is being solicited on a brand name only basis. Please see the attached Statement of Work and Brand Name Determination for additional information. The following solicitation document, incorporated provisions, and clauses are in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2026-01, effective 13 MAR 2026. This solicitation is advertised as a 100% small business set aside, under NAICS Code: 334514 - Totalizing Fluid Meter and Counting Device Manufacturing, with a size standard of 850 employees. title: Radiographic Testing (RT) of a large aluminum weldment
description: SOURCES SOUGHT/REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FOR Radiographic Testing (RT) of a large aluminum weldment for Letterkenny Army Depot (LEAD) The Army Contracting Command, Redstone Arsenal � Letterkenny Army Depot (ACC-RSA-LEAD) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) and Source Sought announcement to gain information from industry and seek sources capable of and interested in providing radiographic testing (RT) of a large aluminum weldment, approximately 14x11x4 FT and thickness of weld joints 1.5-2.0� (more in some locations). All services will be expected to be performed at LEAD. Service provider will be expected to travel to LEAD within 24 hours notice to perform RT operations. Requirements could range in service timeline required and could be subject to daily needs or perhaps months-long gaps in service. Requirements will be expected to meet list of standards provided. Servicer will be responsible for bringing all required equipment for operation from taking images to evaluating them on-site. Methodology whether film, computer, or digital is permitted and subject to contractor discretion and shot requirements. There will often be real-time need for results with asset production and welding being on-hold until RT is completed. Current production outlook is 18 cabs / units in total. 3 cabs will require 100% RT in compliance with print 12940852 E Redline to include all ~230 shots per cab, even those struck out by the redlines. The other 15 cabs will require RT in compliance with 12940852 E Redline as it is written, ~ 37 shots required per cab. There are provisions in the 12940852 print for sampling plans and rework outcomes which would require additional shots to be taken on failed cab and those that follow. The overall project is expected to span late 2026 through 2031. The purpose of providing this information is to conduct Market Research and identify interested sources capable of inspecting these items. The following prints and standards apply to this requirement: 12472301 12553209 12940852 E Redline ASTM E1742 ASTM E1032 Mil Std 1895B Mil Std 2035A Mil Std 3057 Mil Std 370A The drawings for this requirement is export controlled, Distribution D, which contains unclassified sensitive military data. Only vendors who have a current DD Form 2345 � Military Critical Technical Data Agreement on file with Defense Logistics Information Service (DLIS), recent and acceptable NIST rating and Current DoW contracts are authorized to receive the drawing. Interested vendor(s) may request a copy of the applicable drawing via e-mail. Please contact Mr. Thomas Hall at Thomas.c.hall111.civ@army.mil. Contractors must be properly registered in the Government System for Award Management database (SAM). Offerors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation requirements by calling 1-866-606-8220, or via the Internet at www.sam.gov. Eligibility At this point, the Government requests the response from all interested capable businesses and the applicable NAICS for this requirement is 541380 � Testing Laboratories and Services with a small business size standard of $19 Million. At this time, the Government has made no decisions about whether a full and open competition will occur. Upon receipt of all responses to this notice, the Government will determine its path forward. Capabilities Statement and additional Information and Submission Details REQUESTED INFORMATION: Please provide a Capabilities Statement, which must address the following items: Company Information: Please provide your Company Name, CAGE Code, UEI Number, and physical address of your primary facility. Socioeconomic Status: Based on NAICS Code 541380 (Testing Laboratories and Services), what is your business size? Please list all applicable socioeconomic categories (e.g., Small Business, WOSB, SDVOSB, HUBZone, 8(a)). System for Award Management: Is your company currently registered and active in SAM.gov? Manufacturer vs. Distributor: For this specific requirement, will your company be the Manufacturer of the radiographic testing, or will you be acting as a distributor/dealer supplying the end-item of another manufacturer? Corporate Experience & Capability 5. Company Experience: Describe your company's experience over the last five years in performing radiographic testing (RT) on large aluminum weldments, particularly for military or aerospace applications. Please provide at least two examples of similar projects, including the scope, duration, and customer. 6. On-Site Operations: Detail your experience in setting up and conducting RT operations at a client's facility, specifically at a government or military installation like an Army Depot. 7. Turnaround Time: The requirement states a need for real-time results as asset production will be on hold. Describe your standard process for providing on-site image evaluation and delivering immediate results to production personnel. What is your typical turnaround time from image capture to providing a pass/fail determination? Personnel Qualifications 8. Certifications: Confirm that all personnel who will perform and interpret radiographic tests are certified in accordance with MIL-STD-3057, ASNT CP-189, or NAS410. Please specify which certification(s) your personnel hold and their certification levels (e.g., NDT Level II, Level III). 9. Inspector Experience: Provide details on the qualifications and years of experience of the NDT Level II or Level III inspectors who would be assigned to this project. Specifically, detail their experience with interpreting radiographs of aluminum welds according to military standards like MIL-STD-2035A and MIL-STD-1895. Technical Approach & Equipment 10. RT Methodology: The requirement permits film, computed, or digital radiography. Which method(s) does your company specialize in? Describe the advantages of your proposed methodology for this specific application (large aluminum structure, variable shot requirements). 11. Equipment: Provide a comprehensive list of the equipment you would bring on-site to perform all required tasks, from image capture to on-site evaluation. Include details on the radiation source (X-ray/Gamma-ray), imaging plates/film, processing/scanning equipment, and viewing/evaluation software and hardware. 12. Standards Compliance: Confirm your capability and standard procedures for performing RT in accordance with the following standards: MIL-STD-3057 (Arc Welding of Armor Grade Aluminum) MIL-STD-1895 (Radiographic Procedures for Partial-Penetration Aluminum Welds) MIL-STD-2035A (Nondestructive Testing Acceptance Criteria) ASTM E1742 (Standard Practice for Radiographic Examination) ASTM E1032 (Standard Practice for Radiographic Examination of Weldments Using Film) 13. Shot Execution Plan: Describe your approach to performing the high volume of shots required (approximately 230 shots for the first 3 cabs and 37 for the remaining 15), including how you would manage location marking, setup efficiency, and ensuring full coverage as per print 12940852. Operational & Logistical Capability 14. Rapid Deployment: The government requires service providers to be on-site at Letterkenny Army Depot (LEAD) within 24 hours of notification. Describe your logistical plan to meet this rapid deployment requirement, including personnel and equipment mobilization. 15. Scheduling Flexibility: This project involves an inconsistent workload, with potential for daily needs followed by months-long gaps in service between 2026 and 2031. How would your company manage personnel and resource allocation to accommodate this unpredictable schedule while ensuring availability? 16. Safety Plan: Provide an overview of your company's Radiation Protection Program (RPP) and safety procedures for conducting RT operations on an active production floor, ensuring the safety of both your personnel and nearby government employees. title: CentralSquare Pro Cloud Software and Services
description: NASA�s Information Technology Procurement Office (ITPO) has a requirement for CentralSquare Pro Cloud software and services to support mission?critical Computer?Aided Dispatch (CAD) and Records Management System (RMS) operations for NASA Protective Services. The requirement includes cloud?based CAD dispatch positions, mobile CAD licenses, field operations modules, GIS mapping and AVL playback, GovCloud?hosted CAD and RMS environments, CLQ location services, SMS paging, API connectivity, and CrimeView analytics subscriptions for integrated crime?data analysis. Together, these components provide a unified, secure, AWS?hosted platform that enables real?time dispatching, mobile responder connectivity, NIBRS?compliant reporting, and data?driven situational awareness across all NASA centers. NASA/ITPO intends to issue a sole source contract to acquire the services from CentralSquare Technologies, LLC of 1000 Business Center Drive, Lake Mary, Florida 32746-5585 under the authority of FAR 6.103-1, only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. CentralSquare Technologies, LLC is the sole source provider for this requirement. The Government intends to acquire a commercial product or service using FAR Part 12. title: USFS R6 Consolidated Snowmobile and ATV Purchase
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. Quotes are being requested. The U.S. Forest Service, Region 6, has a requirement for the procurement and delivery of one (1) All-Terrain Vehicle (ATV) and four (4) snowmobiles. All vehicles must be delivered new, fully assembled, fluids serviced, and in a 100% turnkey state ready for immediate field deployment upon arrival to support field operations in the Pacific Northwest (PNW) National Forests. Schedule of Items & Delivery Locations All shipments shall be shipped FOB Destination and contract line item pricing must be fully inclusive of all freight, handling, and delivery charges. CLIN 0001: All-Terrain Vehicle (ATV) Quantity: 1 EA Delivery Location: Hood River Ranger Station, 6780 Hwy 35, Parkdale, OR 97041 CLIN 0002: Snowmobiles (#6120, #6121) Quantity: 2 EA Delivery Location: Deschutes National Forest, Scott Street Compound, 80 SE Miller Ave, Bend, OR 97702 CLIN 0003: Snowmobiles (#6678, #6680) Quantity: 2 EA Delivery Location: Siuslaw National Forest, 1850 NE Four Acre Place, Corvallis, OR 97330 Key Technical Salient Characteristics (see attached salient characteristics for additional specs) General (All CLINs): Brand new only; manufactured in the U.S.; minimum 1-year manufacturer warranty; one operators manual per vehicle. CLIN 0001 (ATV): 4-stroke liquid-cooled gasoline engine (600cc�800cc); automatic CVT transmission with H/L/N/R; selectable 2WD/AWD/4WD; single passenger; min 4.0-gallon fuel tank; weight under 800 lbs; wheelbase under 55 inches; integrated cargo racks; 1.25-inch rear receiver hitch. CLIN 0002 (Snowmobiles): 550cc�650cc liquid-cooled engine; Mandatory factory-installed spark arrestor; minimum 2-person seating; heavy-duty rear utility cargo rack kit compatible with 154-inch track footprint. CLIN 0003 (Snowmobiles): 800cc�850cc 2-stroke liquid-cooled engine (91+ octane premium fuel); Mandatory factory-installed spark arrestor; 1-person seating; minimum 146-inch track length; integrated rear bumper tow package/hitch; dual electric and pull start; grip warmers. Award Structure & Evaluation The Government intends to evaluate quotes using simplified commercial procedures and may make up to two (2) separate Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) awards to achieve the most advantageous solution. Vendors may bid via three options: Option A: CLIN 0001 only (ATV) Option B: CLINs 0002 and 0003 only (Snowmobiles�must price both) Option C: All line items (CLINs 0001 through 0003) Quotes will be evaluated via side-by-side Comparative Evaluation based on the following criteria: Technical Capability & Salient Characteristics Delivery Timeline: Must be delivered within 90 calendar days from the date of award (shorter timelines may be evaluated more favorably). Price: Evaluated for fairness and reasonableness. Submission Instructions Quotation packages must be submitted via email to MINDY HICKMAN at mindy.hickman@usda.gov. Closing Date: Offers must be received no later than September 29, 2026, at 11:00 AM PDT. To be considered for award, the package must contain: SF-1449: Completed and signed (Blocks 17a, 30a, 30b, and 30c). Your Unique Entity ID (UEI) must be included in Block 17a. SF-30 Amendments: Acknowledged and signed copy of any posted amendments. Schedule of Items: Completed pricing using the provided Government form. Technical Documentation: Submit spec sheets, or product brochures for the offered Snowmobiles and ATVs to verify technical acceptability.

title: 6515--DUOLITH Acute Care Shockwave Therapy Device - 518-26-4-7480-0062
description: Combined Synopsis Solicitation for Commercial Products and Commercial Services DuoLith SD1 T TOP Ultra Dual Modality Shockwave Therapy System & OrthoPulse Ultra 100 This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) in FAR 12.202, Streamlined Procedures for Evaluation and Solicitation for Commercial Products and Commercial Services, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested, and a written solicitation document will not be issued. This solicitation is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ). The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through the most recent Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC). Set Aside: UNRESTRICTED (Open Market) NAICS: 334510 Electromedical and Electrotherapeutic Apparatus Manufacturing PSC/FSC: 6515 Medical and Surgical Instruments, Equipment, and Supplies Small Business Size Standard: 1,250 employees Procuring Activity Department of Veterans Affairs Network Contracting Office 1 (New England) 940 Belmont Street, Brockton, MA 02301 Point of Contact: Harris, Sherrye Sherrye.Harris@va.gov Delivery Terms and Address FOB: Destination Delivery Address: VAMC Bedford, 200 Springs Road, Bedford, MA 01730 Required Delivery Date: Vendor to state best achievable lead time. Supplies/Services Line Item 0001 DuoLith SD1 T TOP Ultra Dual Modality Shockwave Therapy System Quantity: 1 Each Description: Dual modality shockwave therapy system on a single platform/cart providing both focused (electromagnetic, FSW) and radial/pressure wave (RPW) delivery; configured for shared clinical use by Pain and Podiatry. Salient Characteristics: Dual modality shockwave on a single platform/cart: BOTH focused (electromagnetic, FSW) and radial/pressure wave (RPW) delivery. Pain and Podiatry use both modalities for different tissue depths and indications; a single modality device would not meet the shared clinical need. Focused source with FDA labeling supporting the chronic plantar fasciitis indication for Podiatry s use (PMA/approval for chronic proximal plantar fasciitis). Focused source parameters: energy flux density approximately 0.01 to 0.55 mJ/mm²; adjustable focal depth via stand offs with focal zones spanning roughly 0 to 65 mm; pulse frequency 1 to 8 Hz. Radial source parameters: pressure approximately 1 to 5 bar; frequency 1 to 21 Hz; includes a standard musculoskeletal radial transmitter/applicator set. Required Components Focused electromagnetic FSW unit F SW Sepia handpiece Standard accessory kit: handpiece bracket; water bag; silicon oil; UltraGel coupling gel; power cord; Stand Off I (30 mm); Stand Off II (15 mm); closing ring; operating manual Mobile stand/cart with second shelf Tablet with stand (system operation) Line Item 0002 OrthoPulse Ultra 100 (Radial/Pressure Wave) System Quantity: 1 Each Description: Radial/pressure wave therapy system for superficial myofascial and musculoskeletal applications. Required Components OrthoPulse configuration (Brand Name or Equal): Radial/pressure wave generator console Falcon D Actor handpiece Radial applicator/transmitter set (9) with case V Actor handpiece Falcon revision set (replacement wear items: tubes and bullets) D Actor handpiece brush EPAT/ESWT patient literature kit Warranty for Items 1 and 2 Minimum 2 year factory warranty for device(s) and compressor Minimum 1,000,000 pulse wear warranty Submission Requirements Technical Submission: Detailed documentation mapping to each salient characteristic above and FDA PMA evidence for the focused plantar fasciitis indication. Authorized Distributor Letter: Documentation from the OEM verifying the Offeror is an authorized distributor for the proposed system(s). Delivery timeline Evaluation Criteria Comparative evaluation will be used under RFO Simplified Acquisition Procedures. Award will be made to the lowest priced, technically acceptable quotation that: Meets all technical requirements and characteristics of the DuoLith SD1 T TOP Ultra (and associated RPW capability) and OrthoPulse Ultra 100 Provides acceptable warranty coverage Provide Items 1 and Item 2 simultaneously Demonstrates authorized distribution (OEM provided letter or documentation) Submission Deadline and Questions Submission Deadline: September 29, 2026 by 7 PM Eastern Time Quotes must be emailed to: sherrye.harris@va.gov. Questions are due no later than September 28, 2026 3:00 PM Eastern Time to: sherrye.harris@va.gov.

title: Ohio Wide Water Testing
description: This is a combined synopsis RFP set aside 100% SDVOSB Firm-Fixed Price IDIQ water testing for Ohio facilities with the Department of Veterans Affairs. The Department of Veterans Affairs has a requirement for water testing sample collection, analysis, and results management for government-owned buildings in which patients, residents, or visitors stay overnight located primarily in Cincinnati, Chillicothe, Columbus, Cleveland and Dayton. We are looking for a contractor to provide these water testing services (similar to a Legionella or SPS/ST108 FFP contract) The expectation is routine weekly, monthly, quarterly testing with additional testing done upon task order between the contractor and Contracting Officer as typical with an IDIQ and the retesting needs that arise with water testing. Contractors are asked to use the Price/Cost Excel sheet to present their price proposals in combination with the RFQ document and to understand the tests that may be required for these services. Review and read all attachments. 9/23/26 2:00 pm EST is deadline to email questions to contracting POCs. Submission deadline of Proposals is 9/29/26 2:00 PM. There will be no site visits.

description: Amendment 0005: An amendment has been made to Solicitation W9123626BA0006. Please see attachment SF30, Solicitation Amendment W9123626BA006_0005. The purpose of this project is to construct 24 concrete turning pads, along with required site drainage improvements and road alignment and repair as necessary. The contract will be executed in three distinct phases, with the contractor granted access to only one phase at a time. Completion of each phase is required before proceeding to the next. The remaining phases (two and three) will only be performed if the options for phases are exercised. During construction activities in one phase, the Army will conduct training operations in the remaining two phases. Each turning pad, as identified in the project drawings, will require excavation of the existing roadbed and placement of concrete in accordance with the design specifications. Storm drainage systems will be installed to ensure positive site drainage throughout the construction process. Upon proper curing of the concrete turning pads, the connecting roads will be regarded and aligned to seamlessly integrate with the pads, as detailed in the contract drawings.

title: Synopsis - Vision Correction Assembly
description: SCOPE: The Army Contracting Command - Detroit Arsenal (ACC-DTA) intends to issue a solicitation for a new five-year, Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract for the manufacture and delivery of the Vision Correction Assembly. NSN 4240-01-631-8044, Part Number: 5-1-4208 This is a non-commercial requirement to be manufactured in accordance with a Government-owned Technical Data Package (TDP). The contract will also include requirements for First Article Testing (FAT), Production Lot Testing (PLT) and other Contract Data Requirements (CDRLs). The Government intends to award a single contract to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best price to the Government. This procurement will utilize Invitation for Bids procedures, detailed under FAR Part 14 Sealed Bidding. TECHNICAL DATA PACKAGE (TDP): The TDP associated with this procurement is export-controlled (Distribution Statement D) and requires special handling. To be eligible to gain access to the TDP when the solicitation is released, interested offerors must have a current and valid DD Form 2345, "Militarily Critical Technical Data Agreement" certification on file with the U.S./Canada Joint Certification Office (JCO). Instructions for obtaining certification can be found at: http://www.dla.mil/HQ/InformationOperations/Offers/Products/LogisticsApplications/JCP.aspx. SOLICITATION RELEASE: The solicitation is anticipated to be released on or around 30 September 2026. title: INVITATION TO SUBMIT AN EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (EOI) - Office Space
description: Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) is asking interested parties to provide information for a potential lease of space that meets the following criteria: Section A: Lease Components • a lease term of approximately 10 years, commencing on or about December 1, 2029, with a right of early termination anytime on or after December 1, 2037 provided written notice is given at least 12 months prior; • approximately 983 usable square metres (um2) of contiguous office space; • approximately 50 um2 of contiguous storage space; basement storage space is preferred; • the proposed space must be available approximately 48 weeks prior to the above-noted lease commencement date so all space(s) may be prepared for occupancy; • the proposed space should satisfy or be capable of satisfying the following criteria: 1. must be within office or commercial type buildings; buildings situated within heavy or medium industrial zoning and industrial type buildings with warehouse or manufacturing space will not be considered. A mixed use building may be considered at the sole discretion of PSPC; 2. proposed space must be contiguous and located entirely on one floor; 3. the dimensions must be compatible for efficient design and use; 4. a minimum floor loading capacity of 10.0 kPa (208.9 lbs. per square foot) for 70 um2 of the above-noted office space requirement; 5. a dedicated telecommunication/equipment room measuring no less than 9.0 um² within the proposed space must be provided; this area will not form part of the Lessee’s usable area noted above but will be included in the rentable area calculation; 6. daytime cleaning must be available; 7. access to a loading area must be available; 8. be fully accessible to persons with a disability; 9. a public transit stop must be within 600 metres of the buildings main entrance, and the frequency of service must not be greater than 30 minute intervals between the hours of 0700 hours and 1800 hours, Monday to Friday inclusive and there must be an accessible walking route between the public transit stop and the building; 10. acceptable space for the installation of a bicycle rack(s); 11. the physical characteristics of the Lands and the Building and the area and environment surrounding it, including neighbouring land uses, shall be compatible with the Lessee’s intended use of the accommodation; • the proposed space must be located in the City of Saskatoon. • on or before the lease commencement date, the proposed space will have to comply with all requirements contained in PSPC’s Standards for Leased Accommodation, a copy of which may be obtained from the contact listed in Section F; Note: PSPC may wish to visit or inspect the proposed space upon reasonable notice and a threat and risk assessment may be undertaken in order to assess potential threats to the security of the proposed space and to the public.

description: Η παρούσα Προκήρυξη αφορά την προμήθεια των εξής ακόλουθων δύο (2) οχημάτων και ενός (1) μηχανήματος έργου: (α) ενός καινούργιου υδροφόρου πυροσβεστικού οχήματος, (β) ενός καινούργιου φορτηγού οχήματος με ανατροπή Μ.Β. έως 3,5 τόνων και (γ) ενός καινούργιου ελαστοχοφόρου φορτωτή, για τις ανάγκες της υπηρεσίας Πολιτικής Προστασίας του Δήμου Αγίου Ευστρατίου.
